theme: The word of God as lamp, loving Scripture
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 119:1-48. This is the longest psalm and the longest chapter in the Bible, and it is a prayer in praise of God’s word. You will read it in four sections over the next week. Today, read slowly, perhaps a few stanzas at a time, and notice the many words for God’s word.
settingTheScene: Psalm 119 is an acrostic. It has twenty-two sections of eight verses each, one for each letter of the Hebrew alphabet, and in each section every verse begins with that letter. The author is not named, though the psalmist speaks as a young man who has faced mockery and affliction. Nearly every verse uses one of eight or so words for God’s revealed will: law, testimonies, precepts, statutes, commandments, rules, word, and promise. It follows Deuteronomy in the plan because the whole book of Deuteronomy is a sermon on loving and keeping God’s word.
observation: “Blessed are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the law of the LORD!” (v. 1).
“How can a young man keep his way pure? By guarding it according to your word” (v. 9).
“I have stored up your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you” (v. 11).
“Open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of your law” (v. 18).
“I am a sojourner on the earth; hide not your commandments from me!” (v. 19).
“My soul clings to the dust; give me life according to your word!” (v. 25).
“I will run in the way of your commandments when you enlarge my heart!” (v. 32).
“Turn my eyes from looking at worthless things; and give me life in your ways” (v. 37). “And I shall walk in a wide place, for I have sought your precepts” (v. 45).
interpretation:
The psalm begins with blessing, and the word is the first word of the Psalter too (Psalm 1:1). The blessed are those who walk in the law of the LORD. This is not a grim path. It is the way of life. The psalmist loves God’s word, and he says so again and again. For him, the law is not an external burden. It is a delight.

Notice the psalmist’s honesty about his need. “My soul clings to the dust.” “Open my eyes.” “Enlarge my heart.” He cannot keep the word by his own strength. He asks God to help him understand it, to love it, and to keep it. The psalm is full of prayer. Reading the Bible is not an exercise in willpower. It is a conversation with God, who must give understanding and desire.

The verse about the young man is among the best-known. How can he keep his way pure? By living according to God’s word. The method is stated in verse 11: “I have stored up your word in my heart.” Memorization and meditation are the way that Scripture shapes behavior. We guard our way by filling our hearts with God’s word, so that when temptation comes, it is already there.

The psalmist also faces opposition. Proud people mock him and princes sit and plot against him. Yet he says that he will speak of God’s testimonies before kings and not be put to shame. His confidence is not in his own reputation, but in the promise. Faith in the word gives courage to speak.

The first section ends with a prayer for freedom: “I shall walk in a wide place.” The world sees obedience as narrow. The psalmist sees it as wide. God’s commands do not confine him. They take him out of the narrow place of sin and into spaciousness.
connection: Jesus said, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and keep it” (Luke 11:28), and “If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples” (John 8:31). He answered temptation with the word of God. Paul says that all Scripture is breathed out by God (2 Timothy 3:16). The psalmist’s prayer to open his eyes is answered when Jesus “opened their minds to understand the Scriptures” (Luke 24:45).
application:
Pick one verse from today’s reading to store in your heart, and write it on a card.

Pray verse 18 before you open your Bible: “Open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things.”

Ask whether you see God’s commands as narrow or wide.
prayerPrompts: Tell God you want to walk in his word and love it.
Ask him to open your eyes to wonderful things in it.
Ask him to store his word in your heart so that you do not sin against him.
